FAQ.q: How far in advance should we book an artist?
FAQ.a: For a headline act, three to six months is comfortable. For smaller shows and corporate events, four to six weeks is usually enough. Festival season fills early, so the sooner you talk to us, the more the line-up is actually a choice.

The artist or crew fee, our coordination, and anything we have listed in writing. Travel, stay, local transport, backline, permits and licences are shown separately at actuals unless we have agreed to bundle them.

FAQ.q: How much do we pay upfront?
FAQ.a: Usually [50%] to confirm the date and the rest before the show, unless the agreement says otherwise. The advance is what actually reserves the artist.

FAQ.q: What happens if the event is cancelled or postponed?
FAQ.a: The advance is non-refundable, and cancelling close to the date can attract up to the full fee. Postponement is possible if the artist and crew are free on the new date. Events beyond anyone’s control are handled under the force majeure clause above.

FAQ.q: Who arranges travel, stay and backline?
FAQ.a: We can arrange everything and bill it at actuals, or you can arrange it to the rider’s specification. Either way, the rider is the standard both sides work to.

FAQ.q: Do you handle music licences like IPRS and PPL?
FAQ.a: The organizer usually holds those licences for the venue and event. We will tell you what is needed, and we can arrange it if you ask us in writing.

FAQ.q: Can we use the photos and videos from our event?
FAQ.a: Yes. Usage is set out in the project agreement, and we will share the files once the work is delivered and paid for. We also keep the right to show the work in our own portfolio.
